policy_title: Work to Counter Global Rise in Authoritarianism
stated: Work to counter the global rise in authoritarianism by championing the liberal, rules-based international order and supporting international institutions such as the United Nations, the Commonwealth, NATO and the International Criminal Court.

source.quote: Work to counter the global rise in authoritarianism by championing the liberal, rules-based international order and supporting international institutions such as the United Nations, the Commonwealth, NATO and the International Criminal Court.

bearing_set.reason: Explicit support for NATO and countering authoritarianism directly bears on national security and defence posture, which are listed indicators under Safety & Security.

Championing the rules-based international order and supporting the ICC and UN directly bears on due process, rule of law, and democratic rights — the core indicators of O9 — at the international level that shapes the framework under which those norms are upheld globally.

membership_note: The policy's primary material effects are on national security (O5, via NATO and counter-authoritarianism) and on the rule-of-law/democratic-rights framework (O9, via ICC, UN, and the rules-based order). Effects on prosperity (O13, via trade stability) and public finances (O12, via potential defence commitments) are too diffuse and unspecified to clear the non-negligible bar at this level of stated detail.
